root_cause.text: The `__sctp_rcv_asconf_lookup()` function in `net/sctp/input.c` fails to validate that the declared length of an address parameter fits within the actual bounds of the ASCONF chunk before passing it to `af->from_addr_param()`, leading to an uninitialized memory read when processing truncated chunks.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff adds a bounds check `if (sizeof(*asconf) + ntohs(param->p.length) > ntohs(ch->length))` to ensure the entire address parameter lies within the chunk, and the commit message states that the function "only checks that the ASCONF chunk can hold the ADDIP header and a parameter header, then calls af->from_addr_param(), which reads the full address... trusting the parameter's declared length."

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a boundary check to ensure the address parameter lies entirely within the ASCONF chunk to prevent out-of-bounds reads.
intent_record.what: Added a boundary check comparing the combined size of the ASCONF header and the address parameter length against the total chunk length.
intent_record.how: Prevents out-of-bounds memory reads from truncated ASCONF chunks by returning NULL if the parameter extends beyond the chunk boundary.

candidates.rationale: This statement retrieves the address parameter from the ASCONF chunk by casting the memory immediately following the ASCONF header, without validating whether the chunk is large enough to actually contain the parameter.
This statement accesses the parameter's type field (`param->p.type`) before verifying if the parameter lies within the actual bounds of the ASCONF chunk, which can lead to an out-of-bounds read.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function `__sctp_rcv_asconf_lookup` introduced in this commit does not perform any bounds checking on the ASCONF chunk's length before accessing the address parameter. Specifically, it casts `param = (union sctp_addr_param *)(asconf + 1)` and immediately accesses `param->v4.param_hdr.type` and passes `param` to `af->from_addr_param(&paddr, param, peer_port, 0)` without verifying if the chunk is large enough to contain the parameter header or the full parameter data, leading to an uninitialized or out-of-bounds memory read.
